Timing: shot ranges use whole-second truncation of supplied boundary timestamps; the final shot continues to approximately 01:59.4.

Fixed anchors: A = continuous counter, wooden front and customer-side stools; B = kitchen pass-through hatch at the far end; C = coffee-machine/back-worktop wall on the service side; D = windows and booth row on the customer side. Screen-side changes alone are not relocations.
Tracked people: M = gray-haired man in brown jacket; W = woman in blue shirt, white apron and hair bun. Present means visually observed; out of frame does not establish physical absence.
State shot 1: M and W not individually identifiable through the distant windows; sides, facing and actions unassessable.
State shot 2: W present on A service side, in front of C and to the coffee-machine side of B, opposite D; looks down and moves along counter wiping with right hand. M not visible.

State shot 3: W remains between A and C, facing customer aisle, then lifts coffee pot in right hand. M emerges near B, visibly approaches along A customer-side aisle beside D, sits near counter bend and faces W.

State shot 4: M's jacketed arms enter from A customer side; he positions mug and withdraws his hand. W's arm enters from service side and pours, then withdraws pot. Faces and lower bodies cropped; B/C visible in background, D outside crop.
State shot 5: Neither person visible in tight food insert; A tabletop and D booths visible. Placement and facing cannot be inferred from this crop.

State shot 6: M present at A bend, facing camera rather than across toward C; torso lies beyond countertop while legs emerge in front of its wooden face. B remains behind him, C behind/right, D across aisle. Holds mug with both hands. W not visible.

State shot 7: W present at dining-room face of B, facing kitchen/camera and wiping hatch ledge, then looks toward M. M present at distant A counter, leaning over mug; D and entrance behind him. C runs along service side. Camera reversal explains reversed screen orientation.
State shot 8: Neither person visible; exposed A service area, B and C empty. D edge brightens substantially. Dawn transition permits elapsed time rather than requiring instantaneous disappearance.

State shot 9: M present on a stool at A customer side near B, between A and D, facing inward/down toward mug. W present between A and C, first facing back worktop, then visibly turning and approaching M near B.

State shot 10: M remains on A customer side with D behind him, facing W/down at mug. W remains between A and C, in front of B, handling plate and mug; turns toward B carrying plate. No person changes ownership of an ongoing action.

State shot 11: M remains seated between A and D facing counter. W starts on service side near B, moves through the hatch-end area partly obscured by M, and sits beside him on customer side, facing counter. Her complete path around the far end is not exposed well enough to establish a geometry violation.

State shot 12: M and W both present on A customer side with D behind them, W nearer B and M nearer counter bend. Both hold mugs; M turns toward W. B/C largely outside crop. Reverse camera angle accounts for their changed screen positions.

State shot 13: Neither person visible in sunlit A/B/C insert; D supplies stronger sunlight. Their exact stools are not securely localized in this tighter framing; absence and elapsed time remain confounded.

State shot 14: Hands enter around mug and place money on A. A brown sleeve/plaid cuff associates the paying action with M; faces and room anchors B/C/D are cropped. W's presence and any additional hand attribution are uncertain.

State shot 15: M present outside D, walking away from diner toward truck cab. W visible as transparent reflection in D, facing outward from inside; A/B/C not shown. Payment-to-departure edit permits omitted movement.

State shot 16: W physically present inside beside D booths, facing truck, then turning inward; her reflected image remains in D. M outside at truck cab, reaching/opening door. A/B/C outside framing. Reflection is not a duplicate person.

State shot 17: W initially seated on A customer side between A and D, facing C; rises and carries cups toward service side. At 01:52 her torso is inside A while a leg remains outside its solid front. A second matching W is simultaneously visible farther back near B, wiping A; foreground W faces C then walks toward B. M not visible after departure.

Diff shots 1→2→3: exterior-to-interior framing establishes W; M's rear-area appearance is followed by a visible approach around the counter end. No unsupported disappearance or anchor-side exchange established.
Diff shots 3→4→5: coffee action retains the same participants and sides. Food insert crops both people and allows a serving ellipsis; no disappearance finding.

Diff shots 5→6, also comparing shot 3: M's placement at the solid counter bend is physically inconsistent; reported below. Food-serving elapsed time could explain changing seats, but cannot explain body/counter intersection.
Diff shots 6→7: W is newly visible near hatch outside the preceding shot's main action; reversal changes screen positions. No independently supported disappearance or duplicate.
Diff shots 7→8→9: empty-counter/daybreak transition implies elapsed time, allowing W and M to resume at different positions.

Diff shots 9→10→11→12: participants remain identifiable, mug/plate actions retain ownership, W visibly approaches and sits beside M, and reverse angle preserves seating order relative to hatch and windows. Occlusion prevents a firm finding about her route around the hatch end.
Diff shots 12→13→14→15: sunlit insert, payment close-up and departure permit omitted time and movement. Cropping does not prove disappearance; no hand/person substitution established.
Diff shots 15→16: M continues toward cab, W remains indoors; matching image in glass is a reflection.

Diff shots 16→17: W turns from window and is next seated at counter, an ordinary action ellipsis. Within shot 17, the counter crossing and simultaneous second waitress are distinct visible violations reported below.
Assessment limits: all 26 supplied contact sheets inspected chronologically; selected original frames and a short denser extraction used for placement detail. Audio UNASSESSED.

findings.description: After the food insert, the wide shot at 00:36.458 places the man's torso behind the continuous countertop while his bent legs emerge on the customer side of its solid wooden front. The stool row remains outside the counter to his side. This position persists through 00:44 and makes him appear seated through the counter, unlike his normal customer-side seat before the coffee close-up. An elapsed-time edit or camera reversal cannot account for the body intersecting the fixed counter.

In the final wide shot, the waitress rises from a customer-side stool and moves toward the coffee-machine side. At 01:52 her torso is already behind the countertop while her trailing leg remains in front of the solid wooden counter face. She crosses the uninterrupted counter near its bend rather than walking around an end or through an opening.

At 01:52-01:55, the waitress moving to the coffee-machine worktop is visible at the same time as a second matching woman with the same blue shirt, white apron and bun wiping the far counter near the kitchen hatch. Both occupy the room in one continuous wide view; the rear figure is beside the opaque counter/hatch, not a reflection in the window. The scene had tracked one waitress, and no second person's entrance is shown.
